decisions: An edit is a compare-and-swap on content, not a path: the expectation is resolved from (1) the caller's expected_sha256, (2) the version read_file handed this session, (3) the bytes this runtime last wrote, and refused on mismatch. A target that was never read and never written is still a first write, so create-then-edit flows keep working.

The expectation is re-checked immediately before the rename through the same directory descriptor (hash_confined_child), because a check that happens only before the write is exactly the read-then-write race the story exists to close.

read_file hashes the bytes on disk rather than the decoded text, so the digest the agent quotes back as expected_sha256 is the digest the writer compares (no locale/encoding drift between read and write).

The edit ledger is an append-only per-session JSONL under the harness store (O_APPEND + fsync, bounded by rotation) rather than a schema-v4 SQLite table: it is per-session, append-only and bounded, and putting the edit history inside the exported database would duplicate user file metadata there.

Observed versions are durable (atomic JSON index, bounded to 2048 entries) because the agent's transcript survives a restart; downgrading 'I read version X' to 'no expectation' after a restart would silently weaken the guarantee.

A ledger append failure after the bytes are on disk cannot un-write them, so the edit reports edit_transaction=null plus an edit/ledger_failed event rather than claiming a rollback it did not perform.

decisions: Rollback is a durable per-batch journal plus a version-checked inverse patch, never `git reset --hard` / `git checkout -- PATH` / `git stash`: the destructive forms discard the user's uncommitted work and cannot be scoped to a runtime batch without assuming a clean tree at a known commit (ADR-0007).

The journal records the intended step BEFORE the write. The planner decides from bytes on disk, so a step whose write never happened plans as already_reverted (no-op) and a step whose write did happen restores the stored pre-image; recording after the write would lose exactly the step an interrupted run needs.

A refused plan performs no writes at all, including for the individually safe paths: best-effort partial rollback would leave a third state that is neither before nor after, with no record of it. The batch is persisted as unresolved with per-path reasons plus a dry-run plan.

Three-way merge with `post` as the common base is used when the file changed after the batch: hunks that turn post back into pre are applied onto the current text and disjoint user edits survive; a collision with a user edit is a conflict rather than a guess.

The reconciliation gate blocks only on in_flight/uncertain managed-edit actions (write_file/edit_file), because those are the writes rollback could race and its own restores are compare-and-swapped; other tools' unresolved actions are reported as warnings. An unreadable ledger blocks the rollback (fail closed).
Acknowledgement of unresolved actions is an explicit caller decision (acknowledge_unresolved) recorded in the batch notes and the edit/rollback task event, so a silent override cannot happen.

Batch documents are atomic JSON files rather than a new SQLite table: they are small, written and read whole, need no schema migration, and keep the edit history out of the exported database (same reasoning as ADR-0006's edit ledger).
Private module globals in edit_rollback are prefixed _erb_* because the standalone bundle concatenates inlined modules into one namespace; the collision guard test pins that property.
